text:
anya: quick heads-up — saw a weird p95/p99 jump when running the int8 warmstart harness across clouds. AWS and GCP same a100 SKU but different tails, Azure is worse.

seb: ugh, details? script, batch size, quant lib?

anya: small harness: batch=1, seq=1024, quant backend=fbgemm-like (our internal int8 shim), warm cache for 5k tokens then cold start. Using the same model build. 

anya: GCP (us-central1) p95 ~ 42ms, p99 ~ 120ms. AWS (us-west-2) p95 ~ 46ms, p99 ~ 200ms. Azure (westeurope) p95 ~ 60ms, p99 spikes > 600ms.

maia: did you check driver + CUDA stacks? those spikes smell like nv-peer or kernel fallback.

anya: yup. quick `nvidia-smi` from each (trimmed):

```
# GCP
Driver Version: 525.85.12  CUDA Version: 12.1
# AWS
Driver Version: 510.47.03  CUDA Version: 11.8
# Azure
Driver Version: 470.182.03  CUDA Version: 11.4
```

seb: big diff. cuBLAS/driver combo can change launch paths and fallback kernels. Azure's older driver is suspicious.

infra-bot: noted: Azure image uses vendor kernel 5.15.0-1069, AWS uses 5.10-based, GCP 5.15-custom. Also NIC firmware differs.

maia: can you paste a perf trace? even a short profiler sample will help (kernel durations + SM utilization).

anya: attaching a short text dump from our tracing harness (samples collapsed):

```
GCP: conv_kern_x 0.82ms, matmul_kern_fused 1.9ms, memcpy H2D 0.12ms
AWS: conv_kern_x 0.84ms, matmul_sha 2.2ms, memcpy H2D 0.14ms
Azure: conv_kern_x 0.9ms, matmul_fallback 8.2ms, memcpy H2D 0.13ms
```

seb: `matmul_fallback` — that's the smoking gun. cuBLAS falling back to a slower generic kernel on Azure. Could be due to unsupported SM or driver missing specialized kernels.

maia: also check CPU governor/thermal throttling — I saw Azure hosts with conservative governor which can increase kernel launch jitter when host is busy.

anya: good call. host top during spike shows CPU steal and some IRQ storms.

perf-bot: perf suggestion: try forcing `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0` + `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and re-run with our kernel blacklist toggle to force cuBLAS v12 path if available.

anya: tried forcing `LD_PRELOAD` to our newer cuBLAS shim on Azure container — reduced p99 from ~600ms to ~220ms but still noisy.

seb: that's an improvement. Could be a firmware + driver mismatch that prevents the optimized tensor cores path. Any ECC or MIG config differences?

anya: MIG not used. ECC off. Memory bandwidth readouts look nominal. But I did notice a different PCIe link speed on Azure sample (x8 vs x16) for the device under test.

maia: x8 explains reduced throughput but not 4-6x tail. However if combined with fallback matmul and PCIe link, can amplify latency when GC/fragmentation occurs.

anya: experiment plan: 1) repro with pinned kernel/driver combos (provision GCP image but install AWS driver and vice-versa). 2) run microbench for cuBLAS matmul variations. 3) probe PCIe link and CPU governor under load. 4) try larger batch sizes to see tail amortization.

seb: I'll help with step 1 infra snaps. Can you add the exact command lines and the harness env vars?

anya: harness snippet: `./bench --model model.onnx --backend int8_shim --batch 1 --seq 1024 --warm 5000 --iter 20000`
env: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0`

anya: repro commands to install driver: `curl -O aws-driver.sh && bash aws-driver.sh` (internal script). Will try swap on a GCP VM tonight.

maia: also add a run with `--batch 8` and `--prefix-cache 512` — quant warmstart interacts with prefix cache size sometimes causing kernel diversity.

anya: noted. one more curious data point: when we enable our micro-kernel fusion flag (opt-fuse-matmul), GCP sees p99 drop to 90ms, AWS to 110ms, Azure still high ~200-250ms. suggests Azure lacks some kernel optimizations but fusion helps.

seb: for capacity planning: for Azure tail we should provision more headroom (2x) or use larger batch sizes to smooth p99. But this risks increased p50. Tradeoff depends on customer SLO.

maia: agreed. for Dedicated offering, enforce driver+firmware baseline. For hosted we should add region-specific perf profiles and default to model variants with less kernel sensitivity (fp16 fallback).

anya: filing a short issue with perf traces + nvidia-smi + pci output. Will link here once done.

anya: ps — quick pci output snippet: `lspci -vvv | grep -A3 NVIDIA` shows Azure device LinkCap: 8GT/s x8, GCP/AWS show 16GT/s x16.

perf-bot: note: chart link updated: https://grafana.redwood.test/d/model-onboard?panelId=7&orgId=1

maia: thanks — once we have the driver-swapped repro we'll decide on rollout mitigation. :thumbsup:

seb: cool. i'll stand by for the driver swap logs and we can triage kernel symptoms tomorrow.

infra-bot: created infra ticket INF-3421 to run driver parity matrix across regions (includes automated driver install & smoke harness).

anya: thanks all. will post the repro artifacts in INF-3421 and tag you.

(incident-like but low severity thread; short actions: driver parity test, PCIe link check, microkernel fusion eval, capacity sizing note)
